contexts.text: At this day such flow into the other life in troops.
Three droves of a flock lying near it () = the holy things of the Church and of doctrinal things... Droves of a flock = those things which are of the Church, thus doctrinal things.
Because from that well they watered the droves () = knowledge from the Word... Droves = the knowledge of doctrinal things.

Thither were all the droves gathered together () = that all Churches and their doctrinal things are thence derived. Droves = Churches, and also the doctrinal things which are of Churches, which are from the Word.
(Jacob) set for himself droves for himself alone () = the separation of goods and truths from his own power. Droves, to wit, of the flock, = goods and truths.

(Jacob) gave into the hand of his servants drove and drove apart, and said to his servants, Pass over before me, and set a space between a drove and between a drove () = the ordination as to how they would be initiated... A drove = scientifics, also Knowledges, thus doctrinal things. So long as these are in the external man, that is, in its memory... they are signified by the droves given into the hand of his servants... To set a space between drove and drove = to prepare the way for the good which was to be received.
The droves of the flock and of the herd () = interior and exterior goods.
On certain troops of prophets in the Old Testament.
